title: Testing the Control
briefing: The Cold Chain Safety Authority inspects Valtren in eight weeks. Ruth Adeyemi, Compliance Lead, relies on one control to show that temperature excursions are caught: every refrigerated delivery's data logger is downloaded and reviewed within 24 hours.
She has asked the risk team to test whether the control works before the inspector does.

context.text: Your logger-download indicator from the fleet dashboard already hints that downloads run late at some depots.
The Eastfield compressor failure will be in the inspector's file. Ruth needs this control to be solid.

evidence.title: Control description CC-07
body: Owner: depot supervisor. Frequency: every refrigerated delivery. Activity: download the data logger within 24 hours of delivery, review the trace, log any excursion and notify Quality the same day.
Evidence of operation: download timestamp in the logger system; excursion log.

evidence.title: Your test: random sample of 25 deliveries
body: Downloaded within 24 hours: 19. Downloaded after 48-72 hours: 3. Never downloaded: 3.
Two excursions were in the sample; both were found late (day 3), after the stock had been sold on.
Valtren makes about 2,000 refrigerated deliveries a month.

evidence.title: Depot rota notes
evidence.body: All six late or missing downloads fell on the supervisor's days off. There is no named cover. Nothing alerts anyone when a download is late.

evidence.title: Logger health report
evidence.body: All sampled loggers recorded complete traces. No device faults were reported in the period.

evidence.title: Accounts payable sample (noted in passing)
body: While pulling invoices for the control test you notice two Corvane Materials invoices for the same delivery note, DN-7731, 26,400 each, both paid.
Both were approved under the operational emergency route by the COO's office. It is outside the scope of this test.

questions.prompt: What is your conclusion on control CC-07?

options.label: Reasonably designed but not operating: 6 of 25 (24%) late or missed against a tolerance of 0-1
options.feedback: Design and operation are judged separately; operation fails well beyond any tolerable exception rate.

options.label: Partially effective: 19 of 25 downloads were on time and both excursions were eventually found
options.feedback: Most is not enough for a key control behind a zero-appetite risk.

options.label: Effective: 76% on time is a good rate for a manual control spread across six depots
options.feedback: A 24% failure rate on a key control is a failed test.

options.label: Badly designed: a manual download by one supervisor can never be a reliable food-safety control
options.feedback: The design is sound; the operation is not.

questions.prompt: Which root causes does the evidence support?

options.label: The control depends on one person with no cover for days off
Nothing alerts anyone when a download is late
The data loggers are faulty
options.feedback: The logger health report shows complete traces and no faults.

options.label: Drivers are tampering with the loggers
options.feedback: There is no evidence of tampering.

questions.prompt: If the sample is representative, roughly how many deliveries a month are downloaded late or not at all?
questions.explanation: 24% of 2,000 = 480 a month. A small sample, so treat it as an estimate and say so.

mistakes.feedback: 6 is the count in the sample, not the population.
That is 6% of 2,000; the exception rate was 24%.
24 is the percentage, not a number of deliveries.

questions.prompt: What do you recommend before the inspection? Your approval authority is 25,000.

options.label: Automatic dock download with a 4-hour late alert, a named cover on every rota, and a re-test in six weeks (18,000)
options.feedback: Fixes both root causes, stays within your authority, and the re-test gives Ruth evidence for the inspector.

schedules.description: Cold Chain Safety Authority inspection reviews control CC-07

options.label: Re-brief all supervisors on the 24-hour rule and ask depot managers to check compliance weekly
options.feedback: A reminder does not fix missing cover or the lack of an alert.

schedules.description: Cold Chain Safety Authority inspection finds late logger downloads

options.label: Hold the test results back from the inspection pack until the fix is in, then share them with the evidence of repair
options.feedback: Withholding known control failures from a regulator is a serious integrity breach, whatever the intent.

schedules.description: The inspector finds the test results that were left out of the pack

questions.prompt: How do you report the test to Ruth?

options.label: Test, sample and method, exceptions, conclusion, root causes, and each action with owner and date
A short note: the control mostly works, late downloads cluster on days off, a fix is being prepared
options.feedback: Understates a failed test and gives Ruth nothing to show the inspector.

options.label: The sample spreadsheet with exceptions highlighted, so Ruth can draw her own conclusions
options.feedback: Evidence without a conclusion or actions.

lesson: Test operation, not just design. Extrapolate with care, fix root causes rather than symptoms, and never hide a control failure from a regulator.
